name: 2000s Modern Baroque
title: 2000s Modern Baroque
paragraphs: 2000s Modern Baroque is a design trend that emerged in the 2000s and reinterprets elements of the historical Baroque style within a contemporary context. While the term "Modern Baroque" is used, alternative names such as "Postmodern Baroque," "Plastic Baroque," and "Neo-Baroque" have also been proposed to describe this style, which has manifestations in interior design, fashion, and logo design. The aesthetic declined during the Great Recession.

This trend involves a selective borrowing and adaptation of Baroque's opulence and ornamentation, rather than a strict replication of the period's aesthetics. Key characteristics include the use of ornate details, gilded accents, sumptuous fabrics (like velvets and brocades), tapestries, lace, and floral embroidery, often combined with modern lines, clean silhouettes, and contemporary materials.

blocks.text: This article is about the 2000s trend. For other uses, see Preppy (disambiguation).

The 2000s Preppy aesthetic refers to a mainstream fashion style that adapted earlier prep-school and Ivy League influences into a more casual, mall-driven look associated with the early to mid-2000s. It is commonly described through clothing such as polo shirts, fitted cardigans, baby tees, low-rise jeans, pleated miniskirts, blazers, and logo-heavy accessories, often drawn from brands like Abercrombie & Fitch, Hollister, American Eagle, and similar mall labels.

In contrast to the more traditional, restrained version of preppy style, the 2000s interpretation had an emphasis on brighter colors, a youthful silhouette, and a more openly status-conscious presentation. It overlapped with broader early-2000s fashion trends such as denim-heavy casualwear and a polished but relaxed “going out” look, making it both a continuation of older prep traditions and a distinct product of its decade.

This aesthetic is largely based on the brands Abercrombie & Fitch, Hollister, and American Eagle, which were commonly found in American malls during the 2000s, when mall culture was prominent in the mainstream. The uniting concepts behind them were sporty, laid-back interpretations of New England Preppy garments, which were also based on sporty fashions, albeit in a more vintage and "stuffy" context. These brands also incorporated California in their marketing, with connections to Surfer culture and aspirationally attractive models. This is especially true for brands such as Hollister Co. and Pac Sun and with TV shows such as The Hills, Laguna Beach, and The OC.

The defining characteristic of the 2000s Preppy silhouette was an intentional play with proportions, heavily utilizing ultra-low-rise cuts and excessive fabric layering. Low-rise denim jeans, denim miniskirts, and pleated tennis skirts were systematically anchored at the hips rather than at the natural waist, creating an elongated torso. To contrast this low-slung lower half, tops were cropped or tightly fitted.

Layering was an essential stylistic requirement rather than a functional necessity. A quintessential technique involved stacking multiple pastel polo shirts on top of one another, with the collars turned upward ("popped") to reveal contrasting colors underneath. Slim-fit tank tops and camisoles with lace trim were layered beneath fitted cardigans, lightweight blazers, or V-neck sweaters, allowing the contrasting hems and straps to remain visible. Furthermore, the wardrobe relied on a blend of casual athletic wear and tailored pieces. Polo dresses and tailored trench coats offered more structured options, while distressed denim and graphic tees with varsity lettering conveyed a casual nonchalance.

Footwear was split evenly between casual comfort and vintage-inspired classics. For daily or beach-inspired looks, rubber or leather flip-flops and sheepskin Ugg boots (often paired with short skirts in mild weather) were standard. For academic or slightly more formal settings, ballet flats, leather loafers, and white canvas sneakers were preferred. Accessories were minimal but highly standardized to signal wealth. In this case, thick fabric headbands, oversized designer sunglasses, and classic pearl-strand necklaces or stud earrings served as the primary status symbols.

Although it is mostly manifested through fashion, 2000s preppy also has an associated lifestyle, which is usually centered around friends, getting good grades at school, shopping, and spending money. It is classier and doesn't have as much of the hard partying culture as McBling.

blocksZh.text: 本文介绍的是 2000 年代的趋势。关于其他用法，请见“预科生 (消歧义)”。
2000 年代预科生审美是指一种主流时尚风格，将早期预科学校和常春藤盟校的影响融入到 2000 年代初至中期的更加休闲、商场驱动的外观中。它通常通过 Polo 衫、合身羊毛衫、婴儿 T 恤、低腰牛仔裤、褶皱迷你裙、西装外套和带有徽标的配饰等服装来描述，这些配饰通常来自 Abercrombie & Fitch、Hollister、American Eagle 和类似的商场品牌。
与更传统、内敛的预科生风格相比，2000 年代的诠释强调更明亮的色彩、年轻的轮廓和更公开的地位意识表现。它与 2000 年代初更广泛的时尚趋势重叠，例如以牛仔布为主的休闲装和精致但轻松的“外出”造型，使其既是古老的预科传统的延续，又是 2000 年代的独特产品。
历史

这种审美很大程度上基于 Abercrombie & Fitch、Hollister 和 American Eagle 等品牌，这些品牌在 2000 年代的美国商场中很常见，当时商场文化在主流中很突出。它们背后的统一概念是对新英格兰预科生服装的运动、休闲诠释，这些服装也基于运动时尚，尽管是在更复古和“古板”的背景下。这些品牌还在营销中融入了加州元素，与冲浪者文化和极具吸引力的模特有联系。对于 Hollister Co. 和 Pac Sun 等品牌以及 The Hills、Laguna Beach 和 The OC 等电视节目来说尤其如此。
时尚
2000 年代 Preppy 廓形的决定性特征是对比例的有意运用，大量采用超低腰剪裁和过多的面料分层。低腰牛仔裤、牛仔迷你裙和褶皱网球裙系统地固定在臀部而不是自然腰部，从而创造出拉长的躯干。为了与低腰的下半身形成鲜明对比，上衣采用剪裁或紧身设计。

分层是一种基本的风格要求，而不是功能上的需要。一种典型的技术是将多件柔和的 Polo 衫叠在一起，将衣领向上翻（“弹出”）以露出下面的对比色。修身背心和带蕾丝饰边的吊带背心叠搭在合身开衫、轻质西装外套或 V 领毛衣下面，使对比鲜明的下摆和肩带保持可见。此外，衣柜里融合了休闲运动服和定制单品。 Polo 连衣裙和定制风衣提供了更具结构性的选择，而仿旧牛仔布和印有校队字样的图案 T 恤则传达出一种休闲的漫不经心的感觉。
鞋类分为休闲舒适款和复古经典款。对于日常或海滩风格的造型，橡胶或皮革人字拖和羊皮 Ugg 靴子（在温和天气下通常搭配短裙）是标准配置。对于学术或稍微正式的场合，芭蕾平底鞋、皮革乐福鞋和白色帆布运动鞋是首选。配饰数量极少，但高度标准化，以彰显财富。在这种情况下，厚实的织物头带、超大的设计师太阳镜和经典的珍珠串项链或耳钉成为主要的身份象征。
生活方式
虽然2000年代的预科生主要通过时尚来体现，但它也有一种相关的生活方式，通常以朋友、在学校取得好成绩、购物和花钱为中心。它更加优雅，并且不像 McBling 那样具有激烈的派对文化。

blocks.text: 2000s Tuscan Mom is a Y2K-revival aesthetic that emerged on TikTok between 2025 and 2026 and gained popularity in April 2026. It is a fashion and lifestyle trend that retrospectively romanticizes a specific type of upper middle-class life from the early 2000s associated with wealthy Italian-Americans, characterized by warm, earthy tones, draped silhouettes, and Mediterranean-inspired decor and architecture. Though this aesthetic is heavily inspired by popular mom characters on television during the early-to-mid 2000s era, it is also a reinterpretation of the fashion trends that were popular at the time.

The term "Tuscan Mom" first experienced a significant increase in online search popularity between December 27th, 2025 and January 3rd, 2026. It continued to gain traction throughout January before reaching its peak in April and May of 2026. This rise in popularity coincided with the rapid growth of the "#tuscanmom" hashtag on TikTok, where users shared fashion edits, mood boards, collages, and styling guides that helped define and popularize the aesthetic. Videos tagged "#tuscanmom" were frequently accompanied by related hashtags such as "#tuscan," "#2000s," "#nostalgia," and "#nostalgiacore."

By April 2026, mainstream media began taking notice of the trend and covering it. Yahoo, Fortune, Teen Vogue and more published articles describing the aesthetic, examining its origins and cultural appeal, and offering guidance on how to achieve the look.

CARI design archivist Evan Collins explained in an interview with Yahoo that "Tuscan Mom is an amalgam of different luxury lifestyle signifiers from that time period in the 2000s... [with] posts [that] are always showing the various luxurious activities and spaces from the time..." The article asserts that, much like the rest of the Y2K revival we are experiencing now, the 2000s Tuscan Mom trend is a rejection of the monochromatic Millennial minimalism that has been popular since the 2010s, and a return to embracing the bold, maximalist styles of the past.

The color palette for 2000s Tuscan Mom is warm, earthy, and natural. Shades of brown and tan are the basis of this look, accompanied by reds, yellow, black and white, and sometimes purples and pinks. Furnishings and home decor will often have wood or gold accents, or be detailed in animal print, especially cheetah, leopard, and zebra prints.

On TikTok, characters from popular television series are often used as visual references or archetypes for the aesthetic. The most common is Gabrielle Solis from Desperate Housewives, but Julie Cooper from The O.C. and Carmela Soprano from The Sopranos are also prevalent. These videos commonly feature imagery of Tuscan-inspired business interiors from the early 2000s (such as The Cheesecake Factory, Olive Garden, and Panera Bread) or the interiors of Tuscan Rustic-styled homes or television sets. The season of Autumn is also associated with this trend due to their similar color palettes.

Additional motifs commonly associated with the 2000s Tuscan Mom trend include Yankee Candles, Starbucks drinks, bubble baths, spas and hair salons, champagne, and the interiors of luxury cars that have tan/brown leather detailing and wood accents, particularly of Cadillac, Mercedes-Benz, and Lexus cars.
Jeans with bedazzling, rhinestones, or applique designs

blocksZh.text: 2000 年代的托斯卡纳妈妈是一种千年复兴美学，于 2025 年至 2026 年间在 TikTok 上出现，并于 2026 年 4 月流行起来。这是一种时尚和生活方式趋势，回顾性地浪漫化了 2000 年代初与富裕的意大利裔美国人相关的特定类型的上中产阶级生活，其特点是温暖、朴实的色调、垂坠的轮廓以及地中海风格的装饰和建筑。虽然这种审美很大程度上受到 2000 年代初期到中期电视上流行的妈妈角色的启发，但它也是对当时流行的时尚趋势的重新诠释。
历史

“托斯卡纳妈妈”一词在 2025 年 12 月 27 日至 2026 年 1 月 3 日期间在线搜索热度首次显着上升。它在整个 1 月持续获得关注，然后在 2026 年 4 月和 5 月达到顶峰。这种流行度的上升与 TikTok 上“#tuscanmom”标签的快速增长同时发生，用户在该标签上分享时尚编辑、情绪板、拼贴画和造型指南，帮助定义和普及这种审美。标记为“#tuscanmom”的视频经常伴有相关主题标签，例如“#tuscan”、“#2000s”、“#nostalgia”和“#nostalgiacore”。
到 2026 年 4 月，主流媒体开始注意到这一趋势并进行报道。雅虎、《财富》、《Teen Vogue》等发表的文章描述了这种美学，研究了它的起源和文化吸引力，并提供了如何实现这种外观的指导。
CARI 设计档案管理员埃文·柯林斯 (Evan Collins) 在接受雅虎采访时解释道，“托斯卡纳妈妈是 2000 年代那个时期不同奢华生活方式标志的混合体……[帖子]总是展示那个时代的各种奢华活动和空间……”文章断言，就像我们现在正在经历的其他千年复兴一样，2000 年代托斯卡纳妈妈趋势是对千禧一代单色极简主义的拒绝。自 2010 年代以来流行，并回归到过去大胆、极繁主义的风格。
视觉效果
2000 年代托斯卡纳妈妈的色调是温暖、朴实和自然的。棕色和棕褐色是这款造型的基础，搭配红色、黄色、黑色和白色，有时还有紫色和粉色。家具和家居装饰通常采用木质或金色装饰，或带有动物图案，尤其是猎豹、豹子和斑马图案。
在 TikTok 上，流行电视剧中的角色经常被用作视觉参考或审美原型。最常见的是《绝望主妇》中的加布里埃尔·索利斯，但《橘子郡》中的朱莉·库珀《黑道家族》中的卡梅拉·女高音也很受欢迎。这些视频通常以 2000 年代初期托斯卡纳风格的商业室内装饰（例如芝士蛋糕工厂、橄榄园和帕内拉面包）或托斯卡纳乡村风格的住宅或电视机的内部装饰为特色。由于色调相似，秋季也与这一趋势相关。
与 2000 年代托斯卡纳妈妈潮流相关的其他主题包括洋基蜡烛、星巴克饮料、泡泡浴、水疗中心和美发沙龙、香槟，以及带有棕褐色/棕色皮革细节和木质装饰的豪华汽车内饰，尤其是凯迪拉克、梅赛德斯-奔驰和雷克萨斯汽车。

blocks.text: 2000s Yoga Mom is a retrospective microtrend that emerged online through TikTok and Pinterest in early 2026, and reached peak popularity in the spring of the same year. The aesthetic is based on the American cultural archetype from the early 2000s, associated with upper-middle-class suburban mothers who incorporated yoga, Pilates, and wellness as a central part of their identity. It combines 2000s-inspired athleisure, conscious consumption, and a focus on physical, mental, and spiritual self care.

It is closely related to the 2000s Tuscan Mom microtrend that developed simultaneously, both being nostalgic, romanticized views of motherhood in the 2000s. This view is colored by a wistful reminiscence for a world that no longer exists, as the basis for this trend is a way of American life that only existed pre-2008 financial crisis, when wellness began to solidify as an aspirational cultural marker. Though mothers who do yoga still exist, economic hardships, increasing political tensions, constantly changing trends, and an environment full of new, ever-present technology makes the original 2000s Yoga Mom lifestyle nearly impossible to attain in this day and age. As such, this trend can come across as comfortingly regressive -- both yearning for a version of life that cannot be recaptured and willfully ignoring the current-day hardships that make it so.

The original archetype solidified between 2001 and 2008, coinciding with the rise of lifestyle television and the expansion of "healthy chic" consumption. Series like Desperate Housewives and Sex and the City helped establish an image of mature, urban/suburban femininity that was sophisticated yet accessible. On the business front, brands like Lululemon popularized the use of activewear outside the gym, laying the foundation for contemporary athleisure. Simultaneously, media figures like Gwyneth Paltrow promoted a holistic wellness discourse that would later crystallize in projects like Goop. The expansion of boutique yoga studios in American suburbs solidified the practice as a social activity, not just a physical one, where women could congregate and meet other like-minded women. As it was primarily marketed towards women, the field quickly became female-dominated both in practice and profession, despite its male-centered roots.

In early 2026, the 2000s Yoga Mom aesthetic began trending on the social media platform TikTok, and quickly spread to Pinterest and Instagram. This occurred alongside a general uptick in Y2K-styled athleisure, causing some to view this aesthetic as a natural extension of the "model-off-duty" trend that had been popular from 2022 to 2025. Athleisure brands such as NikeSkims, Alo and Adanola had been shifting their designs towards more feminine, Y2K-reminiscent looks for a couple of years, slowly introducing "girlier" color choices and retro styles, namely wrap tops, flare bottoms, and fold-over waist leggings. This, coupled with celebrities like Bella Hadid wearing Y2K-inspired athleisure publicly, and an overall cultural shift towards 2000s-era nostalgia, gave birth to the 2000s Yoga Mom trend. Hashtags such as "#yogamom," "#2000syogamom," and #2000swellnessaesthetic" captioned nostalgic moodboards and outfit styling videos. As of August 2026, the trend has hit its peak in May of 2026,[1] but continues to be relatively popular and has not yet seen the sharp decline that most microtrends do.

This aesthetic values mental and physical discipline, "choosing peace" and positivity, and prioritizing self-care, even going as far as isolating oneself from others to achieve it. It also values balance within life, portrayed through being able to manage a wellness schedule and focus on self-improvement alongside being a capable and attentive mother to (often unpictured) children. There is an aspect of New Age spirituality within this trend, as manifestation and affirmations are often discussed, and crystals and other New Age symbols present themselves in the imagery. This however is a minor part of the aesthetic, more so a byproduct of practicing yoga and not entirely necessary to adopt as a belief system.

2000s Yoga Mom is characterized by a light, airy color palette that prioritizes natural and feminine colors. Sage green and pale pink are the most common, followed by neutrals (black, white, gray, beige, brown) and pastel blue. Other soft pastel shades can be incorporated but do not dominate the videos of this aesthetic.
There are a few visual motifs that recur in 2000s Yoga Mom videos and posts. They include (but are not limited to):
Tea and healthy smoothies and juices
Yoga studios with light wood floors and neutral walls
Yoga mats and other yoga accessories
Scenes of nature (waterfalls, sunshine peeking through trees, calm oceans, streams, etc.)

blocksZh.text: “瑜伽妈妈”是 2000 年代的一种回顾性微趋势，于 2026 年初通过 TikTok 和 Pinterest 在网上出现，并在同年春季达到了流行高峰。这种审美观基于 2000 年代初的美国文化原型，与将瑜伽、普拉提和健康作为其身份核心部分的中上阶层郊区母亲有关。它结合了 2000 年代的运动休闲、有意识的消费以及对身体、心理和精神自我护理的关注。

它与同时发展的2000年代托斯卡纳妈妈微趋势密切相关，都是2000年代怀旧、浪漫化的母性观。这种观点带有对已不复存在的世界的怀念，因为这一趋势的基础是 2008 年金融危机之前才存在的美国生活方式，当时健康开始巩固为一种理想的文化标志。尽管做瑜伽的母亲仍然存在，但经济困难、日益紧张的政治局势、不断变化的趋势以及充满新科技的环境，使得 2000 年代瑜伽妈妈最初的生活方式在当今时代几乎不可能实现。因此，这种趋势可能给人一种令人欣慰的倒退感——既渴望一种无法重获的生活，又故意忽视当今造成这种情况的困难。
历史

最初的原型在 2001 年至 2008 年间得到巩固，恰逢生活方式电视的兴起和“健康时尚”消费的扩张。 《绝望的主妇》和《欲望都市》等剧集帮助塑造了成熟、都市/郊区女性气质的形象，既精致又平易近人。在商业方面，Lululemon 等品牌在健身房外推广了运动服的使用，为当代运动休闲奠定了基础。与此同时，格温妮丝·帕特洛 (Gwyneth Paltrow) 等媒体人物推动了整体健康的讨论，这些讨论后来在 Goop 等项目中具体化。美国郊区精品瑜伽工作室的扩张巩固了这种练习作为一种社交活动，而不仅仅是一种身体活动，女性可以在那里聚集并结识其他志同道合的女性。由于该领域主要面向女性，因此尽管其根源以男性为中心，但该领域很快在实践和职业中都以女性为主。

2026 年初，2000 年代瑜伽妈妈审美开始在社交媒体平台 TikTok 上流行，并迅速传播到 Pinterest 和 Instagram。与此同时，千禧年风格的运动休闲风普遍兴起，导致一些人认为这种审美是 2022 年至 2025 年流行的“模特下班”趋势的自然延伸。NikeSkims、Alo 和 Adanola 等运动休闲品牌几年来一直在将设计转向更女性化、让人想起千禧年的外观，慢慢引入“更少女”的颜色选择和复古款式，即裹身上衣、喇叭裤和折叠腰打底裤。再加上贝拉·哈迪德 (Bella Hadid) 等名人公开穿着受千年虫启发的运动休闲服，以及整体文化向 2000 年代怀旧的转变，催生了 2000 年代瑜伽妈妈趋势。 “#yogamom”、“#2000syogamom”和 #2000swellnessaesthetic 等标签为怀旧情绪板和服装造型视频提供标题。截至 2026 年 8 月，这一趋势已于 2026 年 5 月达到顶峰，[1] 但仍然相对流行，尚未出现大多数微趋势那样的急剧下降。
哲学

这种审美重视精神和身体的纪律，“选择和平”和积极性，并优先考虑自我保健，甚至为了实现这一目标而将自己与他人隔离。它还重视生活中的平衡，体现为能够管理健康计划并专注于自我完善，同时成为一个有能力、细心的孩子（通常是未在照片中）的母亲。这种趋势中有新时代灵性的一个方面，因为经常讨论表现和肯定，并且水晶和其他新时代符号在图像中出现。然而，这只是美学的一小部分，更重要的是练习瑜伽的副产品，并不完全有必要采用作为一种信仰体系。
视觉效果
2000 年代 Yoga Mom 的特点是轻盈、通风的调色板，优先考虑自然和女性化的色彩。鼠尾草绿色和淡粉色是最常见的，其次是中性色（黑色、白色、灰色、米色、棕色）和淡蓝色。可以合并其他柔和的色调，但不会主导这种美学的视频。
有一些视觉主题在 2000 年代的 Yoga Mom 视频和帖子中反复出现。它们包括（但不限于）：
莲花、睡莲
茶和健康的冰沙和果汁
温暖、自然的灯光
瑜伽室配有浅色木地板和中性墙壁
瑜伽垫和其他瑜伽配件
蜡烛
佛像
可重复使用的杯子和金属/玻璃瓶
自然场景（瀑布、透过树林的阳光、平静的海洋、溪流等）
水疗中心和其他以健康为导向的空间

blocks.text: 2010s Bright Kawaii is the wiki-given name for Kawaii trends common on Tumblr and Instagram blogs in the mid-2010s. As a counterpart to 2010s Soft Kawaii, this page describes the aesthetic that utilizes bright colors, video game and anime motifs, anime-inspired fashion, and pixel art.

These are a Western perspective on the concurrent Japanese Yume Kawaii aesthetic, which does not generally include references to anime and gamer culture, which Western Weeaboos incorporated, as well as the creation of Harajuku-inspired clothing with Western brands and DIY styling.

Tumblr accounts are often used as large moodboards, where users reblog or post images that would fit their grander aesthetic. One of the communities during the 2010s (and still to this day) is the Kawaii community, which centers around an aspect of Japanese culture surrounding cute objects.

During the 2010s, there was a rise in knowledge of Harajuku's style tribes due to fashion blogs on the Internet sharing images online. Fairy Kei and Yume Kawaii is one of the main inspirations in this aesthetic, with similarities in color palettes and 80s inspiration.

However, this aesthetic is a Western, Tumblr-focused interpretation of the style. During the mid-2010s, various trends and memes became spread-out across the site, such as Pale Grunge, an emphasis on beverages, simple line drawings, and fashion-specific trends (see below.) Another large influence is Pastel Grunge/Pastel Goth, but this aesthetic in particular utilizes more Japanese pop culture as opposed to solely being a fashion style.

Part of the popularity of this style is that during the 2010s, Western audiences were already familiar with anime such as Sailor Moon. Much of the aesthetic relies on anime visuals, and it is not uncommon to see merchandise or GIFs on blogs. So, this aesthetic has nostalgic appeal to people who grew up with this.

Rather than dying out, the Western interpretation of Kawaii and many images still circulate. While the Pale Grunge and meme-y motifs are no longer viral, this style is credited with influencing E-Girl and the trend evolved into Kawaii Gamer. That being said, it is still common to find the digital art aspects in the video game and anime fandoms.

This style really peaked in popularity in 2018 and was commonly found on Pinterest from the late 2010s to the early 2020s. It typically featured Japanese characters, stars, pastel colors, and cute eyes. It was also closely linked to video games, which at first glance appear cute, and to the stereotypes of female streamers, incorporating many cute trends from YouTube, Tumblr, and Pinterest at the time.

Many of the people involved in this movement were typically otaku, did ASMR, or streamed games, as previously mentioned, and were usually sweet and very attached to plushies of Pusheen, Sailor Moon, or unicorns. This arose because, starting in the last decade, people began to appreciate these soft, silly, pastel-colored characters more. It evolved until its end in the 2020s because the characters associated with the TikTok aesthetic began to label this aesthetic "cringe."
The color palette of the aesthetic relies entirely on pastel colors and utilizes naturalistic photography with bright, natural light.

This aesthetic includes the use of motifs, wherein certain photographic subjects become reproduced on clothing, illustrations, etc. The main ones are peaches, strawberries, and milk, with of course strawberry and peach milks being motifs also.

Beverages in general are also common in this aesthetic. Ramune and fancy bottled water are often in photos, as a common photo format during this time was to be holding a beverage in a cute location, and these two beverages are status symbols; Ramune is imported and novel, and bottled water is a frivolous item that was commonly seen in Soft Grunge.

Another motif most common in the aesthetic is retro video games (thus showing the lineage with Kawaii Gamer.) Rather than the newer aesthetic's association with PC gaming and PC customization, this aesthetic uses handheld and instantly recognizable shapes, such as Xbox controllers, Tamagotchi, Nintendo 3DS, arcade boxes, and Game Boys.

Continuing on this pop culture imagery is the use of anime screenshots on Tumblr blogs of this type. Specifically, magical girl anime such as Sailor Moon and Card Captor Sakura were the subjects, given their pastel and kawaii aesthetics.

All of these above objects are often drawn in digital illustrations by artists. The style can be chibi and use thick lines, or they can be thin and look like a flatter version of real objects. One type of image artists created were collections of kawaii objects and snacks floating in a background, sometimes united by a theme, like "what's in my bag" or "strawberry grocery finds." Often, these artists may also create whimsical worlds, such as jungle ecosystems within a beverage container, themed food that gives power-ups like in video games, or towns with anthropomorphic animals. However, artists can also be sardonic and edgy to contrast the kawaii motifs, often writing sarcastic and rude statements in pastel bubble letters.

blocksZh.text: 2010 年代明亮卡哇伊 (Bright Kawaii) 是维基百科对 2010 年代中期 Tumblr 和 Instagram 博客上常见的卡哇伊趋势的命名。作为 2010 年代“软卡哇伊”的对应，本页描述了利用明亮色彩、视频游戏和动漫主题、动漫风格的时尚和像素艺术的美学。
这些是对日本梦卡哇伊美学的西方视角，通常不包括西方 Weeaboos 所融入的动漫和游戏文化，以及采用西方品牌和 DIY 造型创作原宿风格的服装。
历史
Tumblr 帐户通常被用作大型情绪板，用户可以在其中转发或发布符合其宏伟审美的图像。卡哇伊社区是 2010 年代（至今仍然如此）的社区之一，它以日本文化中可爱的物品为中心。
2010 年代，由于互联网上的时尚博客在网上分享图片，人们对原宿时尚部落的了解有所增加。 Fairy Kei 和 Yume Kawaii 是这种美学的主要灵感之一，其调色板和 80 年代的灵感有相似之处。
然而，这种审美是一种西方的、以 Tumblr 为中心的风格诠释。 2010 年代中期，各种趋势和模因在整个网站上蔓延，例如强调饮料的 Pale Grunge、简单的线条画和特定于时尚的趋势（见下文）。另一个较大的影响是 Pastel Grunge/Pastel Goth，但这种美学尤其利用了更多日本流行文化，而不仅仅是一种时尚风格。
这种风格之所以受欢迎，部分原因是在 2010 年代，西方观众已经熟悉了《美少女战士》等动漫。大部分审美依赖于动漫视觉效果，在博客上看到商品或 GIF 并不罕见。所以，这种审美对于伴随它长大的人来说具有怀旧的吸引力。
西方对卡哇伊的诠释和许多图像并没有消失，而是仍然流传。虽然 Pale Grunge 和 meme-y 主题不再流行，但这种风格被认为影响了 E-Girl，并且这一趋势演变为 Kawaii Gamer。话虽如此，在视频游戏和动漫粉丝圈中发现数字艺术方面仍然很常见。
这种风格在 2018 年真正流行起来，从 2010 年代末到 2020 年代初在 Pinterest 上很常见。它通常以日本人物、星星、柔和的色彩和可爱的眼睛为特色。它还与乍一看很可爱的视频游戏以及女性主播的刻板印象密切相关，融合了当时 YouTube、Tumblr 和 Pinterest 的许多可爱趋势。
正如前面提到的，参与这一运动的许多人都是典型的御宅族，玩 ASMR 或流媒体游戏，而且通常很可爱，对 Pusheen、美少女战士或独角兽的毛绒玩具非常着迷。这是因为，从最近十年开始，人们开始更加欣赏这些柔软、愚蠢、色彩柔和的角色。它一直发展到 2020 年代末，因为与 TikTok 美学相关的人物开始给这种美学贴上“畏缩”的标签。
视觉效果
美学的调色板完全依赖于柔和的色彩，并利用明亮、自然光的自然主义摄影。
这种美学包括主题的使用，其中某些摄影主题被复制在服装、插图等上。主要是桃子、草莓和牛奶，当然草莓和桃牛奶也是主题。
一般来说，饮料在这种审美中也很常见。照片中经常出现弹珠汽水和精美的瓶装水，因为当时常见的照片格式是在可爱的位置拿着饮料，而这两种饮料是身份的象征；弹珠汽水是进口的、新颖的，而瓶装水则是Soft Grunge中常见的轻浮物品。
审美中最常见的另一个主题是复古视频游戏（从而显示出与卡哇伊玩家的血统）。这种审美不是将新的审美与 PC 游戏和 PC 定制联系起来，而是使用手持式和立即可识别的形状，例如 Xbox 控制器、Tamagotchi、Nintendo 3DS、街机盒和 Game Boys。
继续这种流行文化图像的是在此类 Tumblr 博客上使用动漫截图。具体而言，《美少女战士》和《魔卡少女樱》等魔法少女动画因其柔和且卡哇伊的美学而成为主题。

所有这些上述对象通常都是由艺术家绘制在数字插图中。风格可以是赤壁并使用粗线，也可以是细线并看起来像真实物体的扁平版本。艺术家创作的一种图像是漂浮在背景中的可爱物品和零食的集合，有时由一个主题统一起来，例如“我的包里有什么”或“草莓杂货店发现”。通常，这些艺术家还可能创造出异想天开的世界，例如饮料容器内的丛林生态系统、像电子游戏中那样提供能量的主题食物，或者有拟人化动物的城镇。然而，艺术家也可以用讽刺和前卫的方式来对比卡哇伊主题，经常用柔和的气泡字母写出讽刺和粗鲁的陈述。
电视节目
蜜蜂与小狗 (2013)

blocks.text: 2010s Dark Fandom is a retrospectively named internet aesthetic that peaked approximately between 2010 and 2016. It is characterized by a fascination with mental instability, gore, and the "corruption" of innocent media, blending Western Creepypasta folklore with Eastern anime tropes (specifically the Yandere archetype).

The aesthetic traces its origins to platforms like YouTube, DeviantArt, and Facebook (via the Spanish-speaking "Desmotivaciones" site) during an era of the internet that allowed unrestricted access to mature content. Its visuals are defined by an aggressive high-contrast palette of black and blood red, often depicting characters "snapping" or entering a violent, manic trance.

While the style was often dismissed as a teenage "edgy phase," the aesthetic served as a genuine emotional outlet for its predominantly young demographic, allowing them to explore themes of anger, jealousy, and alienation through fictional horror proxies.

The aesthetic emerged from the "Wild West" era of Web 2.0, where algorithmic safety filters were less advanced, allowing shock content to proliferate alongside child-friendly media. This environment birthed the Creepypasta phenomenon; digital folklore and urban legends spread via copy-and-paste text on forums. Stories like "The Russian Sleep Experiment" and characters like "Slenderman" and "Jeff the Killer" became viral cultural icons, with Slenderman peaking in popularity between 2012 and 2014.

Simultaneously, the anime community popularized the "Yandere" trope; a character who is lovingly obsessive to the point of homicidal violence. The character Yuno Gasai from the 2011 anime Mirai Nikki (Future Diary) became the "codifier" of this trope, transcending the series to become a standalone symbol of the aesthetic.

By 2015, the game Yandere Simulator exploded in popularity on YouTube. Although the developer stated the game was intended for an audience aged 18-24, the game's promotion by YouTubers with young fanbases meant a substantial teen and pre-teen audience was drawn to it regardless, confirming the aesthetic's status as a distinct youth phenomenon of the time.
By the late 2010s, the popularity of the aesthetic began to wane due to a combination of cultural shifts and platform changes.

A significant turning event occurred with the 2014 "Slenderman stabbing" incident in Waukesha, Wisconsin. The event, in which two 12-year-olds attacked a classmate to allegedly appease the fictional character, triggered a mainstream moral panic regarding internet horror culture. This brought intense scrutiny to the Creepypasta community from parents and media, forcing a re-evaluation of the "roleplay" aspect of the fandom. The incident broke the immersion of the aesthetic; the blurring of fiction and reality, which had previously been a source of thrill, was now associated with severe real-world consequences.

The rise of "cringe culture" (ironic commentary videos involving mocking behaviors, interests, and fandoms perceived as embarrassing) around 2016 led to a widespread mockery of "edgy" internet behavior. The sincere and melodramatic, if performative, expression of insanity that defined the aesthetic became a target for ridicule, causing many adherents to abandon the style to avoid social stigma. Simultaneously, the pillars of the aesthetic faltered; Creepypasta narratives suffered from oversaturation and a perceived drop in quality, while Yandere Simulator faced prolonged development delays and controversy.

Furthermore, the 2017 YouTube "Adpocalypse" significantly impacted the propagation of the aesthetic. As YouTube's algorithms began to demonetize and restrict violent or "shocking" content to appease advertisers, the production of gore-heavy AMVs and horror-themed edits became financially unviable for creators.

A defining practice of the aesthetic is the "Evil Variant," where bright, cheerful characters from childhood media (such as Pokémon, Sonic the Hedgehog, or My Little Pony) are reimagined in a black-and-red palette to signify their "dark side". Examples include "Zatsune Miku" (a dark fanmade version of Hatsune Miku) and "Dark Link." Characters are frequently depicted with a "shadowed upper face" (obscuring the eyes) or with glowing, dilated pupils to convey a loss of control. The "Jeff the Killer" carved smile is also a recurring motif.

A significant portion of the aesthetic was propagated through "Desmotivaciones" (Demotivational) posters; images set in a black frame with white Times New Roman text. These captions often featured pseudo-philosophical quotes about madness, pain, or the "monster inside." Visuals often include "broken data" effects, such as static, JPEG artifacts, and "Zalgo" text. Hyper-realistic blood splatters are frequently superimposed over 2D anime characters to create a jarring, uncanny effect.

The music associated with this aesthetic included high-energy aggression, melodrama, and lyrical themes revolving around insanity, trauma, and being a "monster." The aesthetic was associated with various genres, ranging from Alternative Rock and Nu-Metal to Vocaloid and Brostep.

Notably, a significant portion of this music was consumed almost exclusively through the Nightcore format (speeding up and pitching up a track). The Nightcore remix style was ubiquitous in the community, as the faster tempo suited the editing style of Anime Music Videos (AMVs) and the higher pitch mimicked the youthful, "anime-esque" vocals associated with the characters.

blocksZh.text: 2010 年代的黑暗粉丝圈是一种回顾性命名的互联网美学，大约在 2010 年至 2016 年之间达到顶峰。它的特点是对精神不稳定、血腥和无辜媒体的“腐败”的迷恋，将西方 Creepypasta 民间传说与东方动漫比喻（特别是 Yandere 原型）融合在一起。
这种审美观的起源可以追溯到 YouTube、DeviantArt 和 Facebook（通过西班牙语“Desmotivaciones”网站）等平台，当时的互联网时代允许不受限制地访问成熟内容。其视觉效果由黑色和血红色的激进高对比度调色板定义，通常描绘角色“突然”或进入暴力、狂躁的恍惚状态。
虽然这种风格经常被认为是青少年的“前卫阶段”，但这种审美为其以年轻人为主的人群提供了真正的情感出口，使他们能够通过虚构的恐怖代理来探索愤怒、嫉妒和疏远的主题。
起源
这种审美产生于 Web 2.0 的“狂野西部”时代，当时算法安全过滤器不太先进，使得令人震惊的内容与儿童友好的媒体一起激增。这种环境催生了“Creepypasta”现象；数字民间传说和都市传说通过论坛上的复制粘贴文本传播。 “俄罗斯睡眠实验”等故事以及“Slenderman”和“杀手杰夫”等角色成为病毒式文化偶像，其中 Slenderman 在 2012 年至 2014 年间人气达到顶峰。
病态热潮
与此同时，动漫界流行了“Yandere”这个比喻。一个对爱情痴迷到暴力杀人的角色。 2011 年动画《未来日记》中的角色由乃·加西 (Yuno Gasai) 成为这一比喻的“编纂者”，超越了该系列，成为美学的独立象征。
到 2015 年，Yandere Simulator 游戏在 YouTube 上爆红。尽管开发商表示该游戏的目标受众是 18 至 24 岁的观众，但该游戏由拥有年轻粉丝群的 YouTube 用户进行推广，意味着无论如何都会吸引大量青少年和青春期前的观众，这证实了这种审美作为当时独特的青年现象的地位。
衰退
到 2010 年代末，由于文化转变和平台变化的结合，这种美学的流行度开始减弱。
2014 年威斯康星州沃克夏发生的“Slenderman 刺伤”事件发生了重大转折。在这起事件中，两名 12 岁的孩子袭击了一名同学，据称是为了安抚虚构人物，引发了对网络恐怖文化的主流道德恐慌。这引起了家长和媒体对 Creepypasta 社区的严格审查，迫使粉丝重新评估“角色扮演”方面。事件打破了审美的沉浸感；虚构与现实的模糊曾经是刺激的源泉，现在却与现实世界的严重后果联系在一起。

2016 年左右，“畏缩文化”（涉及嘲笑行为、兴趣和被认为令人尴尬的粉丝圈的讽刺评论视频）的兴起导致了对“前卫”互联网行为的广泛嘲笑。这种真诚而夸张（如果是表演性的）疯狂的表达定义了这种审美，成为嘲笑的目标，导致许多追随者放弃这种风格以避免社会耻辱。与此同时，审美的支柱动摇了。 Creepypasta 叙事遭受过饱和和质量下降的困扰，而 Yandere Simulator 则面临着长期的开发延迟和争议。
此外，2017年YouTube的“Adpocalypse”对审美的传播产生了重大影响。随着 YouTube 的算法开始取消和限制暴力或“令人震惊”的内容以安抚广告商，制作血腥的 AMV 和恐怖主题的剪辑对于创作者来说在经济上变得不可行。
视觉效果
审美的一个定义实践是“邪恶变体”，其中来自童年媒体的明亮、欢快的角色（例如神奇宝贝、刺猬索尼克或小马驹）被用黑红色调色板重新想象，以表示他们的“黑暗面”。例子包括“Zatsune Miku”（初音未来的黑暗粉丝版本）和“Dark Link”。人物经常被描绘成“上脸有阴影”（遮住眼睛）或发光、放大的瞳孔，以表达失去控制的感觉。 “杀手杰夫”雕刻的微笑也是一个反复出现的主题。
美学的很大一部分是通过“Desmotivaciones”（去激励）海报传播的；图像设置在黑色框架中，带有白色 Times New Roman 文本。这些标题通常包含有关疯狂、痛苦或“内心的怪物”的伪哲学引言。视觉效果通常包括“损坏的数据”效果，例如静态、JPEG 伪像和“Zalgo”文本。超现实的血迹经常叠加在 2D 动漫角色上，创造出一种刺耳的、不可思议的效果。
音乐
与这种审美相关的音乐包括高能量的攻击性、情节剧和围绕疯狂、创伤和成为“怪物”的抒情主题。这种美学与各种流派相关，从另类摇滚和新金属到 Vocaloid 和 Brostep。
值得注意的是，这种音乐的很大一部分几乎完全通过 Nightcore 格式（加速和提高音调）来消耗。 Nightcore 混音风格在社区中无处不在，因为更快的节奏适合动漫音乐视频 (AMV) 的编辑风格，而更高的音调模仿了与角色相关的年轻“动漫式”声音。

blocks.text: The style is a retrospective phenomenon, created by Gen Z looking back on what they consider the "classic era" of meme culture. The aesthetic has been subject to criticism, pejoratively nicknamed "Retroslop" or "Rainbowslop" on some platforms due to its overwhelming and visually loud nature.

The aesthetic itself began to take shape in the early 2020s on platforms like TikTok and Pinterest, where users began creating these maximalist compositions as a form of nostalgia for their "internet childhood" (often described in the form of "POV: you had unrestricted internet access as a kid" anecdotes). The source material for these collages originated on websites like 4chan, DeviantArt, Newgrounds, Tumblr, and early YouTube between roughly 2005 and 2014.

The aesthetic is often mislabeled as Scene, but it is a distinct phenomenon. While Scene was a music-based subculture with roots in post-hardcore and metalcore that often emphasized a lifestyle of internet fame, 2010s Meme Maximalism is a purely internet-native visual style focused exclusively on memes. However, it does have a significant overlap with Scenecore, a 2020s TikTok-based revival that blends elements of the original Scene subculture with the pop culture-heavy visuals of this aesthetic.

The term "2010s Meme Maximalism" was coined on this wiki in 2025. The name is a combination of "2010s" (here referring to the decade it draws its primary inspiration from, rather than its original timespan), "Meme" (for its connection to meme culture) and "Maximalism" (to highlight its visually loud style) and was created to avoid the negative connotations of pejorative terms like "Retroslop."

The intense nostalgia for 2010s internet culture has generated a counter-phenomenon known as the "Great Meme Reset." This is a meta-meme, widely circulated on platforms like TikTok, which predicts that on a specific date (often cited as January 1, 2026), internet culture will undergo a forced stylistic reversion. The movement explicitly calls for the death of modern "brainrot" memes and highly saturated meme trends, demanding a return to the simpler, "dank" meme style of the 2010s.

The visual foundation the 2010s Meme Maximalism aesthetic is the dense collage with little to no negative space. The background is typically a vibrant, chaotic pattern, such as a rainbow gradient, a galaxy print, or brightly colored splatters. This canvas is then layered with a multitude of iconic internet memes from the late 2000s and early 2010s. The most prominent motifs are rage comic faces, including Trollface, Me Gusta, Forever Alone, and the "Y U NO" guy. Other essential visual elements include rainbows (see also Internet Awesomesauce), elements of MLG, Nyan Cat, the Epic Face, early image macros (typically using the Impact font), and "Advice Animal" memes. The aesthetic embraces the often crude, low-resolution, and MS Paint-drawn quality of its source material, valuing nostalgic authenticity over polish.

A common trope within fanart in this aesthetic is the anthropomorphization of iconic internet figures (such as Derpina, Nyan Cat, or the old Roblox Noob). These characters are often reimagined as human or human-adjacent figures wearing exaggerated versions of 2000s alternative fashion, particularly Scene, Scenecore, or Kandi Raver inspired clothing. This includes bright, dyed, choppy hair, studded belts, striped stockings, large bows, and heavy makeup, all rendered in the aesthetic's signature vibrant, chaotic colors.

As this aesthetic gained more visibility, it also faced significant criticism for being perceived as an anachronistic and inauthentic representation of the past. The style is often pejoratively labeled as "Retroslop," a term used to describe what critics see as a messy, overwhelming, and inaccurate attempt to replicate a past era's internet culture, often by people who did not experience it firsthand.

However, followers of the aesthetic contend that the "Retroslop" critique is often a straw man. They argue that the style's goal is not to faithfully recreate the past, but to transmute existing low-fidelity and nostalgic assets into something new and "silly" (in the modern meme context) as a valid form of creative self-expression.

A prominent example of this backlash occurred in early 2025 with the viral song and animation meme, "Don't Touch My Pizza." While initially popular, the song became a target of widespread mockery on TikTok, where it was frequently labeled as "corny" and one of the "worst songs of all time." The negative reception of the song's self-consciously "random" lyrics and 2010s-inspired visual style was a direct manifestation of the "Retroslop" critique, showing a cultural shift where these overt and maximalist displays of nostalgia are viewed by many as forced and inauthentic rather than genuinely appealing.

The music of 2010s Meme Maximalism is not a specific genre, but a collection of songs that became iconic through their association with viral videos, Flash animations, and the "random" humor of the era. The sound is typically high-energy, electronic, and repetitive, and frequently includes elements of nightcore (speeding and pitching up an audio).

blocksZh.text: 这种风格是一种回顾性现象，由 Z 世代创造，他们回顾了他们所认为的模因文化的“经典时代”。这种美学一直受到批评，由于其压倒性和视觉响亮的性质，在一些平台上被轻蔑地称为“Retroslop”或“Rainbowslop”。
历史
这种美学本身于 2020 年代初开始在 TikTok 和 Pinterest 等平台上形成，用户开始创作这些极简主义作品，作为对“互联网童年”（通常以“POV：小时候可以不受限制地访问互联网”轶事的形式描述）的怀旧。这些拼贴画的源材料源自 4chan、DeviantArt、Newgrounds、Tumblr 和大约 2005 年至 2014 年期间的早期 YouTube 等网站。

这种美学经常被错误地标记为“场景”，但它是一种独特的现象。 Scene 是一种以音乐为基础的亚文化，植根于后硬核和金属核，通常强调互联网成名的生活方式，而 2010 年代的 Meme Maximalism 则是一种纯粹的互联网原生视觉风格，专门专注于 meme。然而，它确实与 Scenecore 有很大的重叠，后者是 2020 年代基于 TikTok 的复兴，将原始 Scene 亚文化的元素与这种审美的流行文化视觉效果融为一体。
造币
“2010s Meme Maximalism”这个术语是在 2025 年在这个 wiki 上创造的。这个名字是“2010s”（这里指的是它主要灵感来源的十年，而不是它最初的时间跨度）、“Meme”（因为它与 meme 文化的联系）和“Maximalism”（为了突出其视觉上响亮的风格）的组合，是为了避免像“Retroslop”这样的贬义词的负面含义而创建的。
伟大的模因重置
对 2010 年代互联网文化的强烈怀旧催生了一种被称为“伟大模因重置”的反现象。这是一个元模因，在 TikTok 等平台上广泛流传，它预测在某个特定日期（通常被称为 2026 年 1 月 1 日），互联网文化将经历强制风格逆转。该运动明确呼吁消灭现代“脑残”模因和高度饱和的模因趋势，要求回归 2010 年代更简单、“潮湿”的模因风格。
视觉效果

2010 年代 Meme 极繁主义美学的视觉基础是密集的拼贴画，几乎没有负空间。背景通常是充满活力、混乱的图案，例如彩虹渐变、银河图案或色彩鲜艳的泼溅物。然后，这幅画布上覆盖了 2000 年代末和 2010 年代初的大量标志性互联网迷因。最突出的主题是愤怒的漫画面孔，包括 Trollface、Me Gusta、Forever Alone 和“Y U NO”家伙。其他基本视觉元素包括彩虹（另请参阅 Internet Awesomesauce）、MLG、Nyan Cat、Epic Face、早期图像宏（通常使用 Impact 字体）和“Advice Animal”模因元素。美学包含了其源材料通常是粗糙的、低分辨率的和 MS Paint 绘制的质量，重视怀旧的真实性而不是抛光。

在这种审美中，粉丝艺术中的一个常见比喻是对标志性互联网人物（例如 Derpina、Nyan Cat 或老 Roblox Noob）的拟人化。这些角色经常被重新想象为人类或与人类相邻的人物，穿着 2000 年代另类时尚的夸张版本，特别是受 Scene、Scenecore 或 Kandi Raver 启发的服装。这包括明亮、染色、蓬松的头发、镶钉腰带、条纹长袜、大蝴蝶结和浓妆，所有这些都以美学标志性的充满活力、混乱的色彩呈现。
批评
随着这种美学获得更多关注，它也面临着严重的批评，因为它被认为是对过去的不合时宜和不真实的表现。这种风格经常被轻蔑地称为“Retroslop”，这个术语用来描述评论家认为复制过去时代互联网文化的混乱、压倒性和不准确的尝试，通常是那些没有亲身经历过的人做出的。
然而，美学的追随者认为，“Retroslop”的批评往往是稻草人。他们认为，这种风格的目标不是忠实地再现过去，而是将现有的低保真和怀旧资产转化为新的和“愚蠢的”（在现代模因背景下）的东西，作为创造性自我表达的有效形式。

这种强烈反对的一个突出例子发生在 2025 年初，病毒歌曲和动画模因“别碰我的披萨”。虽然这首歌最初很受欢迎，但后来在 TikTok 上成为广泛嘲笑的目标，经常被贴上“老套”和“有史以来最糟糕的歌曲”之一的标签。这首歌自觉“随意”的歌词和 2010 年代风格的视觉风格所带来的负面评价是“Retroslop”批评的直接体现，表明了一种文化转变，许多人认为这些公开和极端主义的怀旧表现是强迫和不真实的，而不是真正有吸引力的。
音乐
2010 年代 Meme Maximalism 的音乐并不是一种特定的流派，而是一系列歌曲的集合，这些歌曲通过与病毒视频、Flash 动画和那个时代的“随机”幽默的联系而成为标志性的。声音通常是高能量的、电子的和重复的，并且经常包含夜核元素（加快和提高音频的音调）。

blocks.text: 2010s Soft Kawaii is an offshoot of the Kawaii aesthetic based on trends in the 2010s, especially on the website Tumblr. It is largely based on Japanese mascot culture, with the fashion elements being based on Himekaji and Girly Kei fashion trends of the time, as well as Korean fashion. There is also much overlap with 2014 Girly Tumblr.

Because this era coincides with the rise of Instagram, it was common for these photos to have a slightly sepia-toned filter and warmer lighting. The colors most featured in this aesthetic are pink, gray, browns, creams, and mint green. Patterns are also commonly applied to multiple visuals, from phone cases to fashion. English florals and Swiss dots are the most common, lending a more vintage look to the aesthetic.
During this time, the mascots Pusheen the Cat, Rilakkuma, and Domo-kun were especially popular and appeared as plushies, phone cases, and digital stickers.
It was also common for people to create kawaii mascots through attaching facial feature digital stickers to images of food.

The food itself is often sweets in the color palette, such as cupcakes, marshmallows, cinnamon rolls, etc. As a note, the 2010s and the rise of Instagram, foodie culture, and the more widespread use of smartphones can be linked to this photo subject being popular. Because of this, decoden (clay and plastic charms in the shape of food) was a common motif on phone cases, long nails, and headphones.

This aesthetic was also popular amongst Sweet Lolitas, or people who were interested in the fashion but did not participate in it. Because of this, it was not uncommon for street snaps of that era of Lolita and promotional images from Angelic Pretty, a brand often releasing dresses with dessert printed fabric.

The fashion in this aesthetic is a blend of Japanese Girly Kei/Himekaji fashion, Korean preppy trends, and Western Twee. Blogs would both reblog images of these different nations' fashion on one blog and pick and choose different elements and garments depending on price and local availability within their outfit.

The most defining feature of the fashion is the use of collared tops, especially Peter Pan collars with ruffle or lace trim. This garment in particular has always been featured in Kawaii fashion, taking inspiration from Lolita and various retro fashions. Because of its popularity during the 2010s, this top could be found in various places, from simpler designs from fast fashion and more textured and detailed ones from certain brands in Japan.
Often, outfits would layer these blouses under a plainer sweater or sweatshirt, a trend common in the 2010s as a result of Twee.
Another commonly used top in this aesthetic is from Western and Korean brands, featured thicker lace being the main fabric, both with and without collars.

As this is an extremely feminine aesthetic, skirts are the most common option, specifically A-line mini skirts, rather than longer and tighter fitting ones that would fit into a more mature aesthetic. These skirts often have lace trim, pleats, or ruffles to enhance the kawaii detail.

A more fanciful (and expensive) option is printed skirts from Japanese brands such as Liz Lisa, overlapping with Himekaji. Because these prints are really distinctive, and bloggers often hype up specific releases, these skirts are often a status symbol.
However, a more casual interpretation and less overtly Kawaii option is denim short-shorts, with another 2010s trend being non-blue denim.

During the 2010s, shoes tend to be wedge heels, booties, and platform heels. The kawaii motifs came in the form of brogue-like details, pleather bows, and pastel colors that add details to the shoes differing from more mainstream fashion.

blocksZh.text: 2010 年代的软卡哇伊是卡哇伊美学的一个分支，基于 2010 年代的趋势，尤其是在 Tumblr 网站上。它主要基于日本吉祥物文化，时尚元素基于当时的 Himekaji 和 Girly Kei 流行趋势以及韩国时尚。与 2014 年 Girly Tumblr 也有很多重叠之处。
视觉效果
因为这个时代恰逢 Instagram 的兴起，所以这些照片通常具有略带棕褐色调的滤镜和较温暖的灯光。这种美学中最突出的颜色是粉色、灰色、棕色、奶油色和薄荷绿。图案也通常应用于多种视觉效果，从手机壳到时装。英国花卉和瑞士圆点是最常见的，为审美增添了更多复古的外观。
在此期间，吉祥物 Pusheen 猫、Rilakkuma 和 Domo-kun 特别受欢迎，并以毛绒玩具、手机壳和数码贴纸的形式出现。
人们通过将面部特征数字贴纸贴在食物图像上来创建卡哇伊吉祥物也很常见。
食物本身在调色板中通常是糖果，例如纸杯蛋糕、棉花糖、肉桂卷等。需要注意的是，2010 年代和 Instagram 的兴起、美食文化以及智能手机的更广泛使用都可以与这种照片主题的流行联系起来。正因为如此，decoden（食物形状的粘土和塑料饰物）成为手机壳、长指甲和耳机上的常见图案。
这种审美观在甜美洛丽塔（Sweet Lolitas）或那些对时尚感兴趣但不参与其中的人中也很流行。正因为如此，那个洛丽塔时代的街拍和经常推出甜点印花面料连衣裙的Angelic Pretty的宣传图片并不少见。
时尚
这种审美的时尚融合了日本少女系/姬路时尚、韩国预科生潮流和西方粗花呢风格。博客会在一个博客上转发这些不同国家的时尚图片，并根据服装的价格和当地供应情况来挑选不同的元素和服装。
最高额
时尚最显着的特征是有领上衣的使用，尤其是带有荷叶边或蕾丝装饰的彼得潘领。特别是这款服装一直是卡哇伊时尚的特色，从洛丽塔和各种复古时尚中汲取灵感。由于它在2010年代的流行，这种上衣在很多地方都可以找到，从快时尚的简单设计到日本某些品牌的更有质感和细节的设计。
通常，服装会将这些衬衫套在较朴素的毛衣或运动衫内，这是 2010 年代 Twee 的流行趋势。
这种审美中另一种常用的上衣来自西方和韩国品牌，以较厚的蕾丝为主要面料，有领子和无领子。
下装
由于这是一种极其女性化的审美，裙子是最常见的选择，特别是 A 字迷你裙，而不是适合更成熟审美的更长、更紧身的裙子。这些裙子通常有蕾丝饰边、褶皱或荷叶边，以增强卡哇伊细节。
一个更奇特（也更昂贵）的选择是 Liz Lisa 等日本品牌的印花裙子，与 Himekaji 重叠。因为这些印花确实非常独特，而且博主经常大肆宣传特定的发布，所以这些裙子通常是身份的象征。
然而，牛仔短裤是一种更休闲、不那么明显卡哇伊的选择，2010 年代的另一个趋势是非蓝色牛仔布。
鞋
2010 年代，鞋子多为坡跟鞋、短靴和厚底鞋。卡哇伊图案以布洛克风格的细节、仿皮蝴蝶结和柔和的色彩等形式出现，为鞋子增添了不同于主流时尚的细节。

blocks.text: The 2010s Summer Nostalgia aesthetic is a style that romanticizes the cultural mood and imagery of summer experiences during the 2010s, especially between 2013 and 2018. The aesthetic is inherently tied to early social media culture, particularly the peak of Tumblr and the rise of Instagram, which is often perceived as an era of care-free illusion, youthful freedom, and collective happiness. The aesthetic is characterized by a photographic treatment that captures a sense of sun-bleached optimism and vivid saturation.

The summer of 2016 is often cited as the most romanticized year within this aesthetic, frequently referenced in online culture as having "immaculate vibes," despite a notable degree of revisionist history applied to the era.

This aesthetic is a result of the popularization of Instagram, which introduced set filters to people. Here, the set filter allowed for the color enhancement seen in these photos. Multiple celebrities, such as Selena Gomez, Ariana Grande, and Kylie Jenner, participated in documenting their lives, which, being residents of Los Angeles because of their stardom, involved the pool, beach, and imagery associated with Los Angeles. Of course, being celebrities, their demographic of younger women mimicked their photos and aspirational lifestyle.

The aesthetic saw a massive resurgence in late 2025 and early 2026, driven by the "2026 is the new 2016" trend on TikTok, which declared January 1, 2026, as a "reset day" for internet culture. A key driver of this cultural shift was the "Great Meme Reset," a social media trend sparked by TikTok creators urging a return to the playful and "unserious" humor of the 2010s. This led to a spike in searches for the era's trends and the widespread reposting of memes from the period, such as "Arthur's Fist" and the "Damn Daniel" viral video. Visually, the resurgence was marked by the return of heavy, non-minimalist image editing, specifically the viral re-adoption of the "Rio de Janeiro" Instagram filter, which was prized for its ability to replicate the saturated sun-drenched look of the original aesthetic.

The revival also coincided with the ten-year cyclical nature of pop culture trends, aligning with major anniversaries such as the launch of Kylie Cosmetics (which marked the return of the "King Kylie" aesthetic) and the conclusion of the Stranger Things series in 2026. Cultural commentators noted that this trend represented a broader rejection of the "Clean Girl" minimalism of the early 2020s, with users instead favoring the bolder and more expressive styles of the mid-2010s.

The aesthetic is characterized by high exposure, heavy saturation, and a stylized lens flare or sun flare. This technique creates an artificially golden-yellow or sun-bleached look that bathes the scene in vibrant, highly saturated colors like teal, neon pink, and purple. This deliberate manipulation of color and light is key to giving the images their characteristic nostalgic warmth.
The aesthetic primarily documents aspirational summer leisure and coastal life, reflecting a highly commercialized version of the "L.A. Girl" or West Coast aesthetic popular on Tumblr.
The most iconic visual is the palm tree, frequently depicted silhouetted against an intensely colored sunset or sky. Scenery focuses on:
Ocean waves, sandy beaches, pool parties, and pool accessories like large flamingo or swan floaties.
Leisure items scattered on the sand or poolside, such as nail polish, simple jewelry, soda cans (e.g., Dr. Pepper), magazines, and popular candy brands.
The aesthetics of the era are also revived through the use of "Keep Calm" memes, which were ubiquitous during the early 2010s.
The skyline of downtown Los Angeles.
The fashion is a blend of 1990s throwback styles with bright, modern accents, centered around casual, easy-going summer attire.

blocksZh.text: 2010 年代夏日怀旧美学是一种浪漫化 2010 年代（尤其是 2013 年至 2018 年）夏季体验的文化情绪和意象的风格。这种美学与早期社交媒体文化有着内在的联系，尤其是 Tumblr 的巅峰和 Instagram 的崛起，后者通常被视为一个无忧无虑的幻想、青春自由和集体幸福的时代。其美学特点是通过摄影处理捕捉阳光漂白的乐观情绪和生动的饱和度。
2016 年夏天经常被认为是这种审美中最浪漫的一年，在网络文化中经常被称为具有“完美的氛围”，尽管这个时代有相当程度的修正主义历史。
语境

这种审美观是 Instagram 普及的结果，Instagram 向人们引入了设置滤镜。在这里，设置的滤镜可以增强这些照片中的色彩。赛琳娜·戈麦斯 (Selena Gomez)、爱莉安娜·格兰德 (Ariana Grande) 和凯莉·詹纳 (Kylie Jenner) 等多位名人参与记录了他们的生活，因为他们的明星身份而成为洛杉矶居民，其中涉及与洛杉矶相关的游泳池、海滩和图像。当然，作为名人，他们的年轻女性群体模仿了他们的照片和理想的生活方式。

在 TikTok 上“2026 年是新的 2016 年”趋势的推动下，这种审美在 2025 年底和 2026 年初大规模复苏，该趋势宣布 2026 年 1 月 1 日为互联网文化的“重置日”。这种文化转变的一个关键驱动力是“伟大的模因重置”，这是一种由 TikTok 创作者引发的社交媒体趋势，敦促回归 2010 年代的俏皮和“不严肃”的幽默。这导致对该时代趋势的搜索量激增，以及该时期模因的广泛转发，例如“亚瑟之拳”和“该死的丹尼尔”病毒视频。从视觉上看，这种复兴的标志是大量、非极简主义图像编辑的回归，特别是“里约热内卢”Instagram滤镜的病毒式重新采用，该滤镜因其能够复制原始美学中饱和的阳光普照的外观而受到赞誉。
此次复兴也恰逢流行文化趋势的十年周期，与凯莉化妆品的推出（标志着“凯莉王”美学的回归）和《怪奇物语》系列于 2026 年完结等重大周年纪念日相吻合。文化评论家指出，这一趋势代表了对 2020 年代初“干净女孩”极简主义的更广泛拒绝，用户转而青睐更大胆、更具表现力的风格。 2010年代中期。
摄影
其美学特点是高曝光、高饱和度以及程式化的镜头光晕或太阳光晕。这种技术创造了一种人工金黄色或阳光漂白的外观，使场景沐浴在充满活力、高度饱和的颜色中，如青色、霓虹粉和紫色。这种对色彩和光线的刻意操纵是赋予图像特有的怀旧温暖的关键。
主题和风景
这种美学主要记录了令人向往的夏季休闲和沿海生活，反映了 Tumblr 上流行的“洛杉矶女孩”或西海岸美学的高度商业化版本。
最具标志性的视觉效果是棕榈树，它经常被描绘成在色彩浓郁的日落或天空的映衬下的剪影。风景重点：
海浪、沙滩、泳池派对以及大型火烈鸟或天鹅浮标等泳池配件。
散落在沙滩或池畔的休闲物品，例如指甲油、简单的珠宝、汽水罐（例如 Dr. Pepper）、杂志和流行的糖果品牌。
那个时代的美学也通过 2010 年代初期无处不在的“保持冷静”模因的使用而复兴。
洛杉矶市中心的天际线。
时尚
该时尚融合了 20 世纪 90 年代的复古风格与明亮、现代的风格，以休闲随和的夏季服装为中心。

Ariana Grande in her "Yours Truly" era
Victoria's Secret white and pink luggage
Drinks with whipped cream and marshmallows (sweet drinks in general)
Screenshots from old Tumblr celebs' blogs, like Madison Beer or Ariana Grande
Girls chilling with pink comfy pajamas and/or Starbucks drinks

blocks.text: "Alt Kid" redirects here. Not to be confused with alternative fashion and subcultures.

2020 Alt (variously called E-Kid, Alt Kid, or Bunny Hat Kid) is an internet-based youth subculture and fashion style that gained prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic in the early 2020s. Popularized on TikTok (specifically the sub-community known as "Alt TikTok"), the aesthetic aggregates pre-existing alternative styles, functioning as a time capsule of quarantine-era online culture.

The style utilizes a collage-like approach to fashion, drawing heavily from Mallgoth, Scene, and E-Girl/E-Boy aesthetics. It maintains thematic links to anime, video games, and the hyperpop music scene. The community adopted the term "Alt Kid" to replace the gendered "E-Girl" and "E-Boy" labels, aiming for inclusivity while distancing the subculture from negative connotations associated with those earlier terms. Following its initial decline, the aesthetic experienced a brief revival attempt in 2025 under the slogan "2025 is the new 2020."

Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, alternative fashion on TikTok was largely restricted to the polarized E-Girl and VSCO Girl subcultures. The 2020 Alt identity coalesced from these early styles, rapidly mainstreaming previously marginalized queer and neurodivergent youth expressions. This new aesthetic formed in direct opposition to "Straight TikTok," a colloquialism for the platform's default algorithm. Straight TikTok relied on viral dance choreographies and conventionally attractive influencers. In contrast, the "Alt TikTok" community hosted unconventional, experimental content. Users actively policed the boundaries between these two algorithms, frequently utilizing the catchphrase "bestie, we almost lost you to Straight TikTok" to signal in-group solidarity when mainstream content appeared on their feeds. Media observers noted this side of the platform operated as a conscious counterculture, utilizing dramatic makeup and absurdist humor. Sociological analyses compared this dynamic to classic models of social deviance, where Alt users actively rejected mainstream ideals to foster an exclusive identity.

Because the demographic largely consisted of young teenagers confined to their homes without disposable income, the subculture developed a strong DIY component. Participants crafted jewelry from safety pins, stacked handmade kandi bracelets, and repurposed Monster Energy can tabs as faux septum piercings. However, this generated significant internal controversy regarding ethical consumption. Traditional alternative communities heavily criticized 2020 Alt as a fast-fashion micro-trend, arguing that despite the DIY elements, the aesthetic heavily relied on mass-purchasing cheap garments from Amazon, most notably the plush bunny hats, which were quickly discarded into landfills once the trend passed. Despite this friction, the community maintained a highly protective structure, frequently accusing mainstream creators of co-opting a culture meant for marginalized youth when Alt audio tracks went viral.

Music industry analysts initially projected the movement would achieve mainstream crossover success comparable to the mid-2000s third-wave emo boom. The peak of the 2020 Alt aesthetic, however, remained brief. By 2023, the style had largely faded as subsequent internet trends, such as the Y2K revival, gained dominance in youth fashion. In January 2025, former participants attempted a "2020 Revival," creating nostalgic content featuring the era's original fashion and audio tracks. This resurgence collapsed almost immediately due to the political turmoil and algorithmic suppression surrounding the U.S. government's legislative efforts to ban TikTok that same month, stifling the movement's momentum.

The 2020 Alt aesthetic relies on specific cosmetic applications and digital post-processing techniques native to early quarantine-era TikTok. Makeup application centers on heavy, unblended pink blush applied directly across the tip of the nose, paired with exaggerated black winged eyeliner. Users frequently draw additional cosmetic details using liquid eyeliner, such as under-eye dots, faux stitches across the nose bridge, or drawn-on lower eyelashes. A prominent subset of the community adopts extreme, theatrical makeup featuring stark white foundation and black lipstick, directly imitating the aesthetic of musical artist Jazmin Bean.

Photography and video content typically take place in domestic bedroom settings illuminated by colored LED strip lights. Users edit these images with high-saturation filters and overlay them with dense clusters of digital stickers. This digital curation heavily features Sanrio characters like Kuromi, alongside Care Bears, glowing hearts, and pentagrams.

2020 Alt fashion is a pastiche of older alternative subcultures, combining Mallgoth, Scene, and E-Girl elements into a layered maximalist silhouette. Upper-body clothing frequently features oversized graphic T-shirts layered over long-sleeved striped shirts, or heavily distressed, oversized striped knit sweaters. Lower-body garments include pleated mini-skirts, dark cargo pants, or lounge pants featuring pop-culture motifs like The Nightmare Before Christmas. Participants typically layer these over ripped fishnet tights, paired with asymmetrical or striped thigh-high socks. Footwear consists of heavy, high-platform boots with multiple metal heart or strap buckles, heavily utilizing brands like Demonia.

Accessories are layered to create a cluttered appearance, incorporating studded belts, thick silver chains, spiked chokers, and fluffy arm warmers. The plush bunny hat with long, dangling ears is the primary accessory of the era, occasionally customized with devil horns or safety pins. Hair is frequently dyed in bright unnatural colors, including split-dye techniques, and styled with high volume, often brushed forward to obscure the eyes.

An ubiquitous micro-aesthetic on Alt TikTok in 2020. Users would set their profile pictures to screenshots of characters from popular anime (e.g., Hunter x Hunter, Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun, My Hero Academia) or games like Danganronpa. These images were edited with "sparkle" filters, pastel overlays, and soft grain. It signaled membership within the "Alt" community and often indicated that the user was a minor or part of the "anitok" (Anime TikTok) circle.

blocksZh.text: 「另类小子」重定向至此。不要与另类时尚和亚文化相混淆。
2020 Alt（也称为 E-Kid、Alt Kid 或 Bunny Hat Kid）是一种基于互联网的青年亚文化和时尚风格，在 2020 年代初期的 COVID-19 大流行期间获得关注。这种审美在 TikTok（特别是被称为“Alt TikTok”的子社区）上流行起来，聚合了预先存在的另类风格，充当了隔离时代网络文化的时间胶囊。

该风格采用了类似拼贴画的时尚风格，大量借鉴了 Mallgoth、Scene 和 E-Girl/E-Boy 美学。它保留了与动漫、视频游戏和超流行音乐场景的主题链接。社区采用了“Alt Kid”一词来取代性别化的“E-Girl”和“E-Boy”标签，旨在实现包容性，同时使亚文化远离与这些早期术语相关的负面含义。继最初的衰落之后，这种美学在 2025 年经历了一次短暂的复兴尝试，口号是“2025 年是新的 2020 年”。
“直接与另类”二分法

在 COVID-19 大流行之前，TikTok 上的另类时尚主要局限于两极分化的 E-Girl 和 VSCO Girl 亚文化。 2020 年的另类身份融合了这些早期风格，迅速将之前边缘化的酷儿和神经分歧的年轻人表达方式纳入主流。这种新的审美观与“Straight TikTok”直接对立，“Straight TikTok”是该平台默认算法的口语。 Straight TikTok 依赖于病毒式的舞蹈编排和传统上有吸引力的影响者。相比之下，“Alt TikTok”社区则托管非传统的实验性内容。用户积极监管这两种算法之间的界限，当主流内容出现在他们的提要上时，经常使用“闺蜜，我们差点让你输给 Straight TikTok”这样的口号来表示群体内的团结。媒体观察家指出，该平台的这一面是一种有意识的反文化，利用戏剧性的化妆和荒诞的幽默。社会学分析将这种动态与社会越轨的经典模型进行了比较，其中 Alt 用户积极拒绝主流理想以培养排他性身份。
DIY 精神和微趋势争议

由于人口主要由被困在家中、没有可支配收入的青少年组成，因此亚文化发展出了强大的 DIY 成分。参与者用安全别针、堆叠的手工坎迪手镯和重新利用的怪物能量罐标签制作了人造隔膜穿孔的珠宝。然而，这引发了有关道德消费的重大内部争议。传统另类社区严厉批评 2020 Alt 是一种快时尚微趋势，认为尽管有 DIY 元素，但这种审美严重依赖于从亚马逊大量购买廉价服装，尤其是毛绒兔子帽，一旦趋势过去，这些帽子很快就会被丢弃到垃圾填埋场。尽管存在这种摩擦，社区仍保持着高度保护的结构，经常指责主流创作者在另类音轨病毒式传播时采用了一种针对边缘化年轻人的文化。
衰落和 2025 年的复兴尝试

音乐行业分析师最初预计该运动将取得与 2000 年代中期第三波情感热潮相当的主流跨界成功。然而，2020 年另类美学的巅峰期仍然短暂。到 2023 年，随着随后的互联网趋势（例如 Y2K 复兴）在青年时尚中占据主导地位，这种风格已基本消失。 2025 年 1 月，前参与者尝试“2020 年复兴”，创作以该时代原创时尚和音轨为特色的怀旧内容。由于同月美国政府立法禁止 TikTok 所引发的政治动荡和算法压制，这场复兴几乎立即崩溃，扼杀了该运动的势头。
视觉效果
2020 年的 Alt 美学依赖于早期隔离时代 TikTok 原生的特定化妆品应用和数字后处理技术。化妆重点是直接在鼻尖涂抹浓重的、未混合的粉红色腮红，搭配夸张的黑色带翼眼线。用户经常使用液体眼线笔绘制额外的化妆品细节，例如眼下点、鼻梁上的人造缝线或绘制的下睫毛。该社区的一个突出群体采用极端的戏剧化妆容，以纯白色粉底和黑色唇膏为特色，直接模仿音乐艺术家 Jazmin Bean 的审美。
摄影和视频内容通常发生在由彩色 LED 灯条照明的家庭卧室环境中。用户使用高饱和度滤镜编辑这些图像，并用密集的数字贴纸覆盖它们。这个数字策展以黑美等三丽鸥角色为主，还有爱心熊、发光的心和五角星。
时尚

2020 年另类时尚是旧式另类亚文化的模仿，将 Mallgoth、Scene 和 E-Girl 元素融入分层的极简主义轮廓中。上半身服装通常采用超大图案 T 恤搭配长袖条纹衬衫，或严重做旧的超大条纹针织毛衣。下半身服装包括褶皱迷你裙、深色工装裤或带有流行文化图案（如《圣诞夜惊魂》）的休闲裤。参与者通常将其套在破洞的渔网紧身裤上，搭配不对称或条纹长筒袜。鞋类包括厚重的高台靴子，带有多个金属心形或带扣，大量使用 Demonia 等品牌。
配饰层次分明，营造出凌乱的外观，包括镶钉腰带、粗银链、尖刺颈链和蓬松的暖臂器。带有长而悬垂的耳朵的毛绒兔子帽是这个时代的主要配饰，偶尔也会定制恶魔角或安全别针。头发经常被染成明亮的、不自然的颜色，包括分染技术，并且设计成高卷度，经常向前梳理以遮挡眼睛。
闪光动漫头像
2020 年 Alt TikTok 上无处不在的微美学。用户可以将自己的个人资料图片设置为热门动漫（例如《全职猎人》、《厕所花子君》、《我的英雄学院》）或《弹丸论破》等游戏中角色的屏幕截图。这些图像使用“闪光”滤镜、柔和的叠加和柔和的颗粒进行了编辑。它标志着“Alt”社区的成员资格，并经常表明该用户是未成年人或“anitok”（动漫 TikTok）圈子的一部分。

blocks.text: This article is about the contemporary trend. For other uses, see Preppy (disambiguation).

2020s Preppy (also known as simply Preppy, Gen Alpha Preppy, TikTok Preppy, or the Sephora Kid aesthetic) is a fashion and lifestyle aesthetic that emerged on TikTok in the early 2020s. While it shares a name with the traditional Preppy aesthetic rooted in Ivy League collegiate fashion, the 2020s iteration refers to a different visual style popular among tween and teenage girls (Gen Alpha). This contemporary version prioritizes bright colors, expensive athleisure, maximalist accessories, and luxury skincare products.

The aesthetic is characterized by conspicuous consumption and a specific set of "status symbol" items, such as Stanley tumblers and Lululemon belt bags. It often acts as a marker of social status within middle and high school settings.

The original Preppy aesthetic came from the way Ivy League preparatory school students in the Northeastern United States would dress. Historically, this style was influenced by tight social circles and wealthy families who encouraged specific jobs, activities, and mannerisms to indicate status. Unlike Gen Alpha Preppy, this definition is limited to a specific social and regional class, characterized by nautical stripes, cable-knit sweaters, polos, and boat shoes.

However, traces of the original meaning of the aesthetic can still be found in this new usage of the term. For example, the use of tennis-inspired clothing can also be seen in the modern interpretation.

The use of the term "prep" also had its precedent in the 2000s to denote popular girls, rather than ones in the New England upper class. For example, Cher from Clueless and the Plastics from Mean Girls are characters often cited as preppy despite their lack of academic aspirations. This led to the fashion trends of 2000s Preppy, which is a more casual, sexy, and accessible version of the original Preppy aesthetic that could be found in brands in shopping malls.

However, the new Preppy branched out in 2021 with a new look largely based off of certain teen-aged TikTok accounts. This represents a semantic shift where the word has detached from its regional and class-based origins to describe a "girly," trend-focused, and wealthy visual appearance. This linguistic evolution mirrors similar slang shifts, such as the change in the meaning of "hippie" or "emo" over varying decades.

In fact, there are TikToks that are centered around Millennials' and Gen Z's surprise that there is a new meaning, as it lacks the academic or "old money" connotation of previous eras. On social media, the term is occasionally used pejoratively as a synonym for "basic," implying that the wearer blindly follows trends or lacks originality. However, within the subculture itself, being called "preppy" is often received as a compliment denoting that one is stylish, wealthy, and well-groomed.
Many visuals originate from viral TikTok trends, viral TikTok dances, vlogs, and "Get Ready With Me" (GRWM) videos.

A major component of the 2020s Preppy lifestyle is an early interest in complex skincare routines, often referred to as the "Sephora Kid" phenomenon. This involves preteens and children purchasing and using high-end cosmetic products, particularly from brands like Drunk Elephant, Glow Recipe, Bubble, and Sol de Janeiro.

While this behavior has drawn criticism regarding the appropriateness of anti-aging ingredients (such as retinol) for young skin, industry analysts attribute the trend to specific marketing strategies employed by cosmetic companies. Brands popularized within the aesthetic utilize bright, neon packaging, pump-mechanism containers that mimic toys, thus appealing to children, and "slurry" mixing rituals that appeal to tactile sensory play. Consequently, the consumption of these products is driven less by dermatological need and more by the products' status as collectibles and aesthetic objects within the "Preppy" aesthetic.
The 2020s Preppy aesthetic is maximalist, bright, and heavily branded. Unlike the muted or navy tones of traditional prep, this aesthetic utilizes a palette of hot pink, teal, cyan, and neon pastels.

A defining characteristic of the style is the use of "dopamine dressing" motifs. Clothing and accessories frequently feature smiley faces, lightning bolts, hearts, stars, and butterflies. These symbols often appear as chenille patches sewn onto bags or trucker hats. Western influences are also prominent, with pink cowgirl hats and white cowgirl boots integrated into otherwise athletic outfits. The style is intended to project happiness, positivity, and energy.
Photography within the aesthetic often employs bright high-saturation filters or "sun-kissed" editing styles, emphasizing a lifestyle of leisure, vacations, and shopping.

The fashion of 2020s Preppy is a hybrid of "girly" motifs and expensive athleisure. The silhouette typically consists of oversized tops paired with tight athletic bottoms. Key garments include Lululemon "Align" leggings or "Hottie Hot" shorts, flared yoga pants, and Aviator Nation hoodies, which are recognizable by their retro stripe patterns.

For sleepwear and casual home wear, the brand Roller Rabbit is central to the look, specifically pajama sets featuring their signature monkey or heart prints. Footwear prioritizes comfort and brand recognition, predominantly Nike Air Force 1s, Birkenstock sandals/clogs, Uggs, Golden Goose sneakers, or Smiley Face Slippers.

blocksZh.text: 此条目介绍的是当代趋势。关于其他用法，请见“预科生 (消歧义)”。

2020 年代 Preppy（也简称为 Preppy、Gen Alpha Preppy、TikTok Preppy 或 Sephora Kid 美学）是 2020 年代初在 TikTok 上出现的一种时尚和生活方式美学。虽然它与植根于常春藤盟校时尚的传统预科生美学同名，但 2020 年代的迭代指的是在青少年女孩 (Gen Alpha) 中流行的不同视觉风格。这个现代版本优先考虑明亮的色彩、昂贵的运动休闲、极繁主义的配饰和奢华的护肤产品。
这种审美的特点是炫耀性消费和一套特定的“地位象征”物品，例如 Stanley 随行杯和 Lululemon 腰包。它通常在初中和高中环境中充当社会地位的标志。
历史
最初的预科生美学来自美国东北部常春藤联盟预科学校学生的着装方式。从历史上看，这种风格受到紧密的社交圈和富裕家庭的影响，他们鼓励特定的工作、活动和举止来表明地位。与 Gen Alpha Preppy 不同，这个定义仅限于特定的社会和地区阶层，其特点是航海条纹、绞花针织毛衣、马球衫和船鞋。
然而，在这个术语的新用法中，仍然可以找到美学最初含义的痕迹。例如，网球风格服装的运用也可以看到现代的诠释。
“prep”一词的使用在 2000 年代也有先例，用来指代受欢迎的女孩，而不是新英格兰上层阶级的女孩。例如，《独领风骚》中的雪儿和《贱女孩》中的塑料角色尽管缺乏学术抱负，但经常被认为是预科生。这引发了 2000 年代 Preppy 的时尚潮流，这是原始 Preppy 美学的更休闲、性感、更平易近人的版本，可以在购物中心的品牌中找到。
然而，新的 Preppy 于 2021 年拓展了业务，其新外观主要基于某些青少年的 TikTok 账户。这代表了语义上的转变，这个词已经脱离了其地域和阶层的起源，用来描述“少女”、注重潮流和丰富的视觉外观。这种语言的演变反映了类似的俚语转变，例如几十年来“嬉皮”或“情绪”含义的变化。
事实上，有些 TikTok 的核心是千禧一代和 Z 世代对它有新含义的惊讶，因为它缺乏以前时代的学术或“旧钱”内涵。在社交媒体上，这个词偶尔被贬义地用作“基本”的同义词，暗示佩戴者盲目追随潮流或缺乏原创性。然而，在亚文化本身中，被称为“预科生”通常被视为一种赞美，表示一个人时尚、富有、打扮得体。
许多视觉效果源自病毒式传播的 TikTok 趋势、病毒式传播的 TikTok 舞蹈、视频博客和“与我一起准备”(GRWM) 视频。
“丝芙兰小子”现象
2020 年代预科生生活方式的一个主要组成部分是对复杂护肤程序的早期兴趣，通常被称为“丝芙兰小子”现象。这涉及青少年和儿童购买和使用高端化妆品，尤其是 Drunk Elephant、Glow Recipe、Bubble 和 Sol de Janeiro 等品牌的产品。
虽然这种行为引起了人们对抗衰老成分（如视黄醇）是否适合年轻皮肤的批评，但行业分析师将这一趋势归因于化妆品公司采用的特定营销策略。在美学中流行的品牌利用明亮的霓虹灯包装、模仿玩具的泵机械容器来吸引儿童，以及吸引触觉感官游戏的“浆液”混合仪式。因此，这些产品的消费较少受到皮肤病学需求的驱动，而更多地受到产品作为“预科生”美学中的收藏品和审美对象的地位的驱动。
视觉效果
2020 年代的预科生审美是极繁主义、明亮且品牌化。与传统预科的柔和或海军色调不同，这种美学采用了亮粉色、青色、青色和霓虹粉彩的调色板。
该风格的一个决定性特征是使用“多巴胺着装”图案。服装和配饰经常以笑脸、闪电、心形、星星和蝴蝶为特色。这些符号通常以雪尼尔补丁的形式出现，缝在包或卡车司机的帽子上。西方的影响也很突出，粉色女牛仔帽和白色女牛仔靴融入了其他运动服装中。这种风格旨在传达快乐、积极和能量。
审美中的摄影常常采用明亮的高饱和度滤镜或“阳光亲吻”的剪辑风格，强调休闲、度假和购物的生活方式。
时尚
2020 年代的预科生时尚是“少女”主题和昂贵运动休闲的混合体。廓形通常由超大上衣搭配紧身运动下装组成。主打服装包括 Lululemon “Align” 紧身裤或“Hottie Hot” 短裤、喇叭形瑜伽裤和 Aviator Nation 连帽衫，其复古条纹图案极具辨识度。
对于睡衣和休闲家居服，Roller Rabbit 品牌是造型的核心，特别是带有其标志性猴子或心形印花的睡衣套装。鞋类优先考虑舒适度和品牌知名度，主要是 Nike Air Force 1、勃肯凉鞋/木底鞋、Uggs、Golden Goose 运动鞋或笑脸拖鞋。

name: Bauhaus
title: Bauhaus
paragraphs: The Bauhaus (full name: Staatliches Bauhaus) was a revolutionary German art school founded by architect Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919. Operating until 1933, it became the most influential school of modern art, design, and architecture in the 20th century. Its core objective was to break down the traditional distinctions between fine arts (like painting and sculpture) and applied arts (like furniture making and textiles) and to unify all creative disciplines into a single "total work of art," or Gesamtkunstwerk. The Bauhaus aimed to create a new type of designer who could create functional, beautiful, and mass-producible objects for the modern industrial age.

The school's philosophy was famously guided by the principle "form follows function," which dictated that the design of an object should be primarily determined by its purpose, free from any unnecessary ornamentation. Unlike the preceding Arts and Crafts movement, which rejected industrialization, the Bauhaus embraced the machine and sought to harness technology for social good. Aesthetically, the Bauhaus is known for its use of clean lines, simple geometric forms (circles, squares, triangles), and a palette often restricted to primary colors (red, yellow, blue), black, and white. Its innovative curriculum began with a preliminary course (Vorkurs) that taught students the fundamentals of materials, color theory, and composition before they entered specialized workshops.

The Bauhaus operated in three locations during its fourteen-year existence: Weimar (1919-1925), Dessau (1925-1932), and Berlin (1932-1933). Each phase was led by a different director—Gropius, Hannes Meyer, and finally Ludwig Mies van der Rohe—and had a distinct focus. The school was ultimately forced to close under pressure from the Nazi regime, which viewed its progressive, internationalist modernism as "degenerate art." Despite its short lifespan, its legacy was immense. Faculty and students emigrated worldwide, spreading Bauhaus ideals that profoundly shaped the development of the International Style in architecture, as well as modern graphic, industrial, and furniture design.
